text:
Using plain water for bladder washout risks osmotic lysis of red blood cells and urothelial irritation, and with fluid absorption can cause hemolysis, hyponatremia, and hypervolemia. The main danger is hemolysis and electrolyte disturbance from hypotonic fluid absorption, especially with prolonged or high-volume irrigation or mucosal injury. Sterile normal saline or the prescribed irrigation fluid should be used instead.
